summary: @workoscalif/sudoku ships opaque 33.6 MB Go binary executed at postinstall while README claims a 34 kB C-compiled ELF
details: package.json declares scripts.postinstall = 'node scripts/postinstall.mjs'. On linux-x64, that script spawns vendor/gridgen-linux-x64 unconditionally during `npm install`. README.md states the shipped binary is a 34 kB static ELF built from native/gridgen.c (a ~10 KB C sudoku generator included in the tarball). The actual file is ~33.6 MB and its strings show the Go runtime (chacha8, GODEBUG, godebugs.Info, tzdata, runtime., reflect., bisect-*, memprofile) — not a compiled-C artifact. The binary is therefore not built from the shipped source, and the README's size and language claims act as a cover story that discourages inspection. Because the binary runs at install time with the installer's user privileges, and its actual behavior (network, filesystem, exec) is opaque and unconstrained by the small Node wrapper that only parses three lines of its stdout, installing this package executes attacker-controlled bytes of unverifiable purpose on the host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
